WISH_09_NEU_5.text: Recognition in the coming year begins with how you see yourself. In this Steady Year, the push and the pull run even, so the way you judge yourself colors how others see you. At the end of each day, say one thing you did well out loud.

WISH_09_OPENFB_2.text: No single year in the next five opens wide for recognition, so steadily built skill, not the winds overhead, shapes how you're seen. Things lean a little toward recognition in {{가까운해}}. Until then, seek out chances to teach or share what you've learned.

WISH_09_OPENFB_3.text: Recognition draws closest in {{가까운해}}, though no clear Open Year appears in the next five. So instead of waiting for applause, hold yourself to your own standards. That's the ground real recognition grows from.

WISH_09_OPENFB_4.text: The next five years ask you to build trust layer by layer rather than wait for a tailwind. Recognition comes most easily in {{가까운해}}, so until then, keep your commitments one by one, all the way through.

WISH_09_OPENFB_5.text: Five years out, the sky shows no strong tailwind for recognition, so learning to recognize yourself matters most. In {{가까운해}}, that self-recognition starts to win recognition from others too. Build the habit now: at the end of each week, name what you did well.

WISH_09_OPEN_2.text: The recognition you've hoped for comes through clearly in {{열리는해}}. With {{근거}}, people notice what you've built that year, and you step into new roles with ease. Until then, choose one piece of work that truly represents you and polish it. By that year, you'll know exactly what story to tell about yourself.

WISH_09_OPEN_3.text: {{열리는해}}, with {{근거}}, is when your efforts earn the recognition they deserve. That year, raise your hand for roles you've wanted and share your ideas boldly. Before then, write a short paragraph that explains your work in plain terms, so you're ready when opportunity knocks.

WISH_09_OPEN_4.text: When {{열리는해}} comes around, {{근거}} draws people's eyes to your work. Use that year to share what you've achieved and announce your next goal out loud. Meanwhile, keep the efforts of the people beside you in mind. Remembering them makes that year's recognition feel even warmer.

WISH_09_OPEN_5.text: Across the next five years, recognition arrives most warmly in {{열리는해}}. Thanks to {{근거}}, that year is perfect for bringing long-prepared work out into the world. Before then, practice sharing even small wins with the people around you, so stepping into the light feels natural when the time comes.

WISH_10_FAV_2.text: Being yourself blossoms in the coming year, an Open Year. With {{근거}}, your tastes and values come into focus, and showing them feels far more natural. Start a little journal that's all yours, filled with photos or notes about the things you love. Being yourself isn't about proving you're different from everyone else, so savor getting to know yourself at your own pace.

WISH_10_FAV_3.text: Thanks to {{근거}}, the coming year is an Open Year for finding your way back to yourself. Feelings you shelved to meet other people's standards rise again, and what you truly want comes into focus. Start with something you see every day, like your wardrobe or your room, and change one thing to suit your own taste. Small choices like that add up to days that feel unmistakably yours.

WISH_10_FAV_4.text: If you long to live on your own terms, the coming year stands firmly in your corner. It's an Open Year for being yourself. With {{근거}}, you find the courage to speak in your own voice and work your own way. Choose one small personal project and keep at it, savoring the process more than the result.

WISH_10_FAV_5.text: Curious about who you really are? The coming year arrives as an Open Year for being yourself. Because of {{근거}}, new experiences reveal sides of you that you never knew were there. Once a month, pick a book or a place you'd normally pass by. As you try the unfamiliar, notice what feels right and what doesn't. That's how your sense of self grows steadfast.

WISH_10_HEAD_2.text: The coming year is a Building Year, a time to strengthen your sense of self from the inside rather than display it. With {{근거}}, tasks and responsibilities come first, and your own wants slip down the list. Once a week, write ‘What do I want right now?’ in a notebook and answer it. Asking that question again and again, even under pressure, builds a center that stays with you.

WISH_10_HEAD_3.text: With {{근거}} at play, the coming year is a Building Year that puts being yourself to the test. Other people's expectations and real-world limits make doing things your way a challenge. Rather than fighting for everything, choose one thing you won't compromise on and hold it fast. That one thing, kept under pressure, becomes the root of who you are.

WISH_10_HEAD_4.text: If you're hoping to be more yourself, the coming year is a Building Year, when progress moves at a slower pace. As {{근거}} brings plenty of demands to meet, time for what you love shrinks. Tuck the things you enjoy into small pockets of time, like your commute or the minutes before sleep. The tastes you protect in those spare moments become a thread that keeps you, you, long after the busy year ends.

WISH_10_HEAD_5.text: Measured against your wish to be yourself, the coming year is a Building Year, when responsibilities step to the front. Because of {{근거}}, you often find yourself meeting standards someone else set, and that feels stifling. Write down three values you truly cherish in work and life, and turn to them whenever you face a decision. The values that sharpen this year become a compass that keeps you true, whatever path you take.

WISH_10_NEU_2.text: For being yourself, the coming year is a Steady Year. The support and the weight balance out, so the rhythm of your days decides whether your sense of self sharpens or fades. Once a week, claim two or three hours alone for something you love.

WISH_10_NEU_3.text: If being yourself is the goal, this is a Steady Year: your choices, not the sky, clear the way. Neither force pulls ahead, so a little courage to say no to what doesn't feel right makes a big difference. This month, politely decline one request you're not up for.

WISH_10_NEU_4.text: Being yourself, in the coming year, grows out of small preferences rather than big resolutions. With the sky leaning neither way in this Steady Year, the little things you insist on each day shape who you are. Once a day, choose something entirely your way, like your morning playlist or your lunch.

WISH_10_NEU_5.text: Your sense of self in the coming year rests on the choices you hold, just as the name Steady Year promises. The push and the pull run even, so the more honest you are with yourself, the clearer your direction becomes. Before bed, recall one moment today when you felt like yourself and one when you didn't. And if the year turns into a Moving Year, that motion can even help you discover a new side of yourself.

WISH_10_OPENFB_2.text: No year in the next five opens wide for being yourself, so time spent looking inward, not the winds overhead, sets your direction. Things tilt a little toward being yourself in {{가까운해}}. Until then, guard some time alone once a week.

WISH_10_OPENFB_3.text: Being yourself comes closest within reach in {{가까운해}}, though no clear Open Year appears in the next five. So skip the big resolutions. Make one small choice each day completely your own way, and let your sense of self grow from there.

WISH_10_OPENFB_4.text: Let the next five years be about sharpening your own standards, little by little, rather than waiting for a tailwind. Being yourself comes most easily in {{가까운해}}, so until then, write down a few values you hold dear and revisit them often.

WISH_10_OPENFB_5.text: Even looking five years out, no year brings a strong tailwind for being yourself, so honesty with yourself becomes your key practice. In {{가까운해}}, that honesty starts showing up in real choices. Begin now: practice saying ‘no’ to things you're not up for.

WISH_10_OPEN_2.text: The sense of self you've hoped for comes into sharp focus in {{열리는해}}. With {{근거}}, that year invites you to follow the choices you're truly drawn to rather than the ones others expect. Until then, jot down your likes and dislikes whenever you notice them, so you choose with confidence when that year arrives.

WISH_10_OPEN_3.text: {{열리는해}}, with {{근거}}, is when showing who you are starts to feel natural. Use that year to launch the personal project you've put off or try a new way of expressing yourself. Before then, carve out a little more time alone and practice listening to your own voice.

WISH_10_OPEN_4.text: Once {{열리는해}} comes around, {{근거}} brings the shape of the life you want into view. That year, reset your priorities in work, relationships, and daily life with ‘does this feel like me?’ as your guide. In the meantime, keep a running list of things that light you up, and that year's choices will feel much lighter.

WISH_10_OPEN_5.text: Of all five years ahead, {{열리는해}} is when your true self shines brightest. Thanks to {{근거}}, that year is perfect for sharing with the world the way of doing things you've quietly held onto. Before then, make even small decisions by your own standards, and you'll meet that year's big choices your own way too.

WISH_11_FAV_2.text: The coming year opens wide for a new start: it's an Open Year. With {{근거}}, you discover surprising possibilities in new kinds of learning and places you've never been. Sign up for an intro class in something you've always wanted to learn, and show up for the first session. The lighter you start, the longer it lasts, so don't wait to have everything figured out.

WISH_11_FAV_3.text: Thanks to {{근거}}, the coming year is an Open Year for new beginnings. Plans you've hesitated over for ages roll along smoothly once you take that first step. Seek out stories from people already doing what you want to try, or reach out and ask them directly. Starting is a joy, so set aside time to wrap up what you already have going, too.

WISH_11_FAV_4.text: If you've dreamed of a fresh start, the coming year throws the door wide open. It's an Open Year for new beginnings. With {{근거}}, supportive people step into your path and opportunities find you, even when everything is new. Widen your usual orbit by one step: wander an unfamiliar neighborhood or drop in on a group you've never joined.

WISH_11_FAV_5.text: If there's something you've longed to start from scratch, the coming year is an Open Year for a new start. Because of {{근거}}, the butterflies outweigh the fear, and the current keeps cheering you on after your first step. Mark the moment: open a fresh notebook and write the person you hope to become on the first page. Several paths open at once, so choose the one that pulls at your heart most and start there.

WISH_11_HEAD_2.text: The coming year is a Building Year, a season for preparing the ground where your new start will grow. With {{근거}}, requirements and responsibilities catch your eye first whenever you try to begin. Do a ‘test run’: practice what you want to start on a small scale. The prep and practice you put in this year become the cornerstone that makes your new start last.

WISH_11_HEAD_3.text: With {{근거}} in play, the coming year is a Building Year, and your new start moves slower than you hoped. Each time you reach for the first step, another hurdle appears, and that wears on you. All the more reason to shrink your start and focus on the smallest bit of prep you can do today. The grit you build clearing each hurdle carries you down the long road once you're on your way.

WISH_11_HEAD_4.text: Your dream of a fresh start meets a Building Year in the coming year, a time to catch your breath at the starting line. As {{근거}} leaves you carrying the weight of finishing what's already on your plate, launching something new takes extra effort. Choose one loose end and tie it up neatly before the year is out. Finishing well makes your next start lighter and steadier.

WISH_11_HEAD_5.text: Let's be honest: the coming year doesn't simply fling open the door to a new start. Because of {{근거}}, it's a Building Year, when you check off the conditions for starting one by one. Talk with people already in the field you want to enter, and gather real-world information ahead of time. The knowledge and connections you gather now become a map that keeps you on course once you set out.

WISH_11_NEU_2.text: For a new start, the coming year is a Steady Year. The support and the weight balance out, so how long you keep going after the first step matters more than when you take it. Break what you want to begin into ten-minute pieces, and do it just three times this week.

WISH_11_NEU_3.text: If you're ready for a fresh start, this is a Steady Year, and you choose the moment you set out. Neither force pulls ahead, so you decide when you're ready. Cut your list of ‘I'll start once I have…’ conditions down to one, and write it down. If the year turns into a Moving Year, that motion gives your first step an extra nudge.

WISH_11_NEU_4.text: New beginnings in the coming year spring from small actions, not from waiting. It's a Steady Year, and the sky tilts neither way, so the simple fact that you took a first step outweighs how big it was. Collect small everyday firsts: take a different route, or order a dish you've never tried.

WISH_11_NEU_5.text: The key to a fresh start sits in your own hands in the coming year. That's the nature of a Steady Year, where the push and the pull run even. Find one person to begin something with, and promise to cheer each other through those first steps.

WISH_11_OPENFB_2.text: Across the next five years, no year opens wide for a new start, so your courage to keep trying small things, not the winds overhead, decides when you set out. Things lean a little toward new beginnings in {{가까운해}}. Until then, try something unfamiliar once a season.

WISH_11_OPENFB_3.text: {{가까운해}} brings a new start closest, though no clear Open Year appears in the next five. So instead of a grand launch, start small and keep it going. That's what protects a fresh start over the long run.

WISH_11_OPENFB_4.text: For the next five years, fill in the prep you need one step at a time instead of waiting for a tailwind. New beginnings come most easily in {{가까운해}}, so until then, choose one skill you'll need to get started and keep honing it.

WISH_11_OPENFB_5.text: No strong tailwind for a new start appears anywhere in the next five years, so your power to open the door yourself matters most. That door swings open more easily in {{가까운해}}. Get ready now: decide which of your current projects to wrap up first.

WISH_11_OPEN_2.text: The fresh start you've hoped for swings its door wide open in {{열리는해}}. With {{근거}}, that year invites you to dive into new kinds of work and learning. Until then, give the fields that interest you a quick test drive, so you know which path to choose when that year comes.

WISH_11_OPEN_3.text: {{열리는해}}, with {{근거}}, makes it far easier to turn long-held plans into action. That year, open yourself to new places, new people, and new roles. Before then, sort what you're doing now into what to wrap up and what to keep, and your fresh start will feel much lighter.

WISH_11_OPEN_4.text: By {{열리는해}}, {{근거}} melts away your doubts about a new start. That year, begin something new for real, even if it's small. In the meantime, start setting aside the time and money you'll need to get going.

WISH_11_OPEN_5.text: {{열리는해}} is the year, out of the next five, when the door to a new start opens widest. Thanks to {{근거}}, that year is made for stepping out of your comfort zone and moving forward. Before then, collect plenty of small firsts, so that year's big leap feels less like stepping into the unknown.

PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p1_how: Before you say 'yes' to a new request, separate what you can do now from what's a stretch. Then say it plainly: 'I can finish this part this week, and the rest by next week.'
PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p1_title: Define how much help you can offer
PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p1_why: You have more choices than all or nothing. Spell out what you can take on, and your coworkers can plan around it with ease.
PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p2_how: Block off one short stretch of focus time on your calendar and give it to a single task. Name it 'Focus time' so you honor it.
PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p2_title: Carve out a short, meeting-free block for yourself
PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p2_why: Guarding your time is boundary work too. Clear space on your calendar lets you breathe, even when requests pour in.
PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p3_how: As you wrap up work, tidy your files, jot down tomorrow's first step, and close every window. Let that be your signal that the workday is over.
PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p3_title: Make closing your last file your end-of-day ritual
PRAC_BOUND_CAREER.p3_why: Draw a clear line between work and rest, and far less work follows you home. You decide when your day ends.

PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p1_how: On a single page, list the people and tasks you've been tending to in your family lately, and mark whether each feels more like 'something I chose' or 'something I took on.' This week, share or scale back one thing you took on.
PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p1_title: Sort the people and tasks you look after into 'chosen / taken on,' and lighten one
PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p1_why: Caring for family comes from love. Protect what you chose, lighten what you took on, and your kindness lasts for the long run.
PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p2_how: When someone at a family gathering makes a joke or asks a question that makes you uncomfortable, and it feels safe, say so briefly: 'I'm not really comfortable with that topic.' Keep the line ready in advance so it comes easily.
PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p2_title: Say in a few words how an uncomfortable joke landed
PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p2_why: Family or not, you have every right to draw a line at hurtful comments. Keep it short and calm, and you stand up for yourself without harming the relationship.
PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p3_how: When a long stretch with family starts to feel stifling, say you're stepping out for fresh air and walk around the block. Decide ahead of time when you'll be back, and you'll relax more easily.
PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p3_title: Take a quick walk around the block to reset
PRAC_BOUND_FAMILY.p3_why: Stepping away for a moment protects the relationship too. As you walk, your body loosens, and you return with room to talk.

PRAC_BOUND_GROWTH.p1_how: Write down one career goal on your mind and mark where its standard came from: your parents, your workplace, social media, or you. Then rewrite it in your own words, something like 'For the life I want, this is enough.'
PRAC_BOUND_GROWTH.p1_title: Ask 'Whose standard is this?' about a goal you're clinging to, then rewrite it in your own words
PRAC_BOUND_GROWTH.p1_why: You get to define what a good life looks like. Simply asking whose standard you're following draws a line between other people's expectations and your own.
PRAC_BOUND_GROWTH.p2_how: When you sit down to study or grow, put your phone out of reach and tell the people you live with: 'Please don't interrupt me for a bit.' Even a short stretch counts when it's truly yours.
PRAC_BOUND_GROWTH.p2_title: Claim uninterrupted time, even a sliver
PRAC_BOUND_GROWTH.p2_why: Asking others to respect your time is boundary-setting too. Every uninterrupted hour you claim builds trust in the promises you make to yourself.
PRAC_BOUND_GROWTH.p3_how: Pick one app or account where other people's wins are always in your face, and schedule days off from it. When comparison kicks in, simply notice 'I'm comparing again.' That noticing is the whole practice.
PRAC_BOUND_GROWTH.p3_why: Comparison quietly turns other people's pace into your yardstick. Limit what you take in, and you protect your own rhythm.

PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p1_how: Jot down how often you like to text or talk with a partner or someone new, and which situations start to feel like too much. Keep one kind, simple sentence ready to explain it when the moment comes.
PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p1_title: Write down how often you like to stay in touch
PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p1_why: Know your own rhythm first, and you can share it with grace. With your words ready, you speak up before hurt feelings pile up.
PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p2_how: Beyond the plans you make together, tell each other about one block of time that matters to you alone: a workout, a night out with friends, an evening to yourself. Anything counts.
PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p2_title: Share the personal time you each want to protect this month
PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p2_why: Knowing each other's plans in advance means fewer hurt feelings. Even in a close bond, boundaries that protect you keep love comfortable for the long haul.
PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p3_how: Choose one activity that delights you, love life aside, and keep it going this week. A solo hobby or plans with friends both count.
PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p3_title: Keep doing what recharges you outside the relationship
PRAC_BOUND_LOVE.p3_why: When other parts of your life fill you up, you don't need your partner to be everything. That breathing room is your strength for holding healthy boundaries.

PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p1_how: Put one small money rule you want to keep for yourself into a single sentence. The more specific the better: 'If someone asks to borrow money, I'll sleep on it before I answer.'
PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p1_title: Write down one everyday rule you want to keep
PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p1_why: Set a rule in advance, and you waver less when someone asks for a favor or something catches your eye. That one line holds the boundary for you.
PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p2_how: Pick one impulse purchase you keep making and fill in four boxes: the pros and cons of buying it, and the pros and cons of letting it go. Save it on your phone, and when the urge returns, read it before you check out.
PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p2_title: Fill in a four-box pros and cons list for an impulse
PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p2_why: Put what you want right now beside what your future self wants, and the choice gets clearer. Setting limits on spending isn't denying yourself. It's taking care of yourself.
PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p3_how: Write down a few things that cost next to nothing yet still lift your mood. The simpler the better: a walk, a favorite song, an afternoon at the library.
PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p3_title: List easy, low-cost things that make you happy
PRAC_BOUND_MONEY.p3_why: If shopping is your only way to cheer up, spending limits are hard to keep. Stock up on easy, low-cost joys, and pushy requests and temptations lose their pull.

PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p1_how: Think of one time you turned down a friend or a group invite and felt good about it, then write down what that 'no' protected. Something small, like rest, your schedule, or your energy, is plenty.
PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p1_title: Recall a recent 'no' you're glad you said
PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p1_why: Guilt tends to linger after you say no. Name what you protected, and the next no feels lighter.
PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p2_how: Write one polite message in advance for days you'd rather rest, and save it in your notes app. Short is best: 'I'm going to sit this one out, but I'd love to catch up next time!'
PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p2_title: Keep a short 'can't make it' message ready
PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p2_why: Scrambling for a no on the spot puts you under pressure. With a message ready, you hold to your decision instead of getting swept along by guilt.
PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p3_how: Pick one evening this week and leave it free of plans. That night, messages can wait.
PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p3_title: Make one people-free evening your small ritual
PRAC_BOUND_SOCIAL.p3_why: Even if you love people, you need time alone to recharge. One free evening lets you savor time with friends on the other days.

PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p1_how: Write down two tasks from this week side by side: one you handled on your own, and one you carried alone that you could easily have shared. Beside the second, add the name of a coworker you'll ask next time and the one sentence you'll say to them.
PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p1_title: Write 'what I handled solo' beside 'what I could have asked for'
PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p1_why: Leaning on others for everything wears you out, and so does carrying it all yourself. Credit yourself for what you've done, plan what to ask for, and reaching out stops feeling like a leap.
PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p2_how: When you hit a wall at work today, don't wrestle with it alone for ages. Ask a coworker a quick question. The smaller the question, the better the practice.
PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p2_title: Admit what you don't know, and ask
PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p2_why: Every small question teaches you that asking is safe. As that sense grows, asking for bigger help feels lighter, too.
PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p3_how: If work has been weighing on you, tell a coworker or friend you trust something simple, like 'This job has been a lot lately.' You don't need them to fix anything.
PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p3_title: Don't bottle it up: say it out loud
PRAC_LEAN_CAREER.p3_why: Putting a heavy feeling into words lightens its weight. It also reminds you that someone stands beside you, ready to be leaned on.

PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p1_how: Starting with family, write down the people who come to mind. Beside each, note how close you are, whether you can lean on them, and whether you can raise hard topics with them. Then star just the one person who's been on your mind most lately.
PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p1_title: Map the people around you and star the one on your mind
PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p1_why: Putting everyone on one page shows you who you lean on now and who you want to draw closer to. A short list is perfectly fine.
PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p2_how: If you've been worrying over a family matter alone, mention it to one family member you feel at ease with, something like 'This has been on my mind lately.' You don't need an answer ready. Your only goal is to open the conversation.
PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p2_title: Don't carry it alone: start by mentioning it lightly
PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p2_why: With family especially, you tend to keep worries to yourself so no one else frets. Bring it up lightly, and you discover this is a bond you can truly lean on.
PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p3_how: When a happy memory with your family surfaces, send it to them in a short message. Add a photo for a warm touch.
PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p3_title: Share one memory you made together
PRAC_LEAN_FAMILY.p3_why: Revisiting good times together draws you closer, even when no one needs anything. Moments like these build up and make leaning on each other easier when life gets hard.

PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p1_how: Pick one place you're stuck in your studies or plans, and ask yourself: 'If I knew how, would I do it?' If the answer is not knowing how, write down one person or resource to ask. If it's anxiety, write one line about what you told yourself in that moment.
PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p1_title: Sort what's blocking you: 'don't know how' or 'feeling anxious'
PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p1_why: Being stuck rarely means you're not good enough. Usually it just means there's something left to learn. Once you name what you need, you see exactly who to turn to.
PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p2_how: Find one person who excels at their work yet clearly enjoys life, and casually ask how they divide their day among study, work, downtime, and sleep. Write their day next to yours, then shift just the one block that differs most.
PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p2_title: Ask someone with high standards and an easy calm how they spend their day
PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p2_why: You can't always judge your own standards from the inside, so borrow another set of eyes. Use their day as a reference point, not a template, and you'll find your balance faster.
PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p3_how: Recall a moment when studying or prep kept you from resting, and write down your 'reasons I can't rest.' Then choose a time when a short break is fine, and take it for real. When thoughts pop up as you rest, simply label them 'to-do thoughts' and let them drift by.
PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p3_title: List your 'reasons I can't rest,' then rest anyway
PRAC_LEAN_GROWTH.p3_why: Trying to do it all yourself pushes even rest off the list. Giving yourself time to rest is how you practice leaning on yourself.

PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p1_how: Make three columns: hugs and attention, listening and understanding, and having your back. In each, write one line about what you'd love from your relationship right now. Then choose one and turn it into words you can actually say to your partner or someone close.
PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p1_title: Write one line each for warmth, understanding, and support
PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p1_why: Once you can name whether you crave warmth, understanding, or support, you know exactly what to ask for. A named need is far easier to voice than a vague sense of being let down.
PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p2_how: When loneliness or emptiness creeps in, write one line: 'Right now, I need connection.' Then offer yourself one kind sentence that doesn't judge the feeling. After that, make one small connection you can manage today, like texting someone to see how they're doing.
PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p2_title: Feeling lonely? Write 'I need connection,' then reach out in one small way
PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p2_why: Loneliness isn't a flaw. It's a signal that you need connection. Acknowledge it, answer it in small ways, and your ability to lean on others grows steadily.
PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p3_how: Take turns telling your partner one thing that feels like pressure on a rough day and one thing that truly helps. Jot down each other's answers so they're ready when you need them.
PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p3_title: Discover how each of you likes to be supported
PRAC_LEAN_LOVE.p3_why: Encouragement lands differently for everyone. Tell your partner ahead of time what comforts you, and leaning on them on a hard day becomes so much easier.

PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p1_how: When money or everyday worries weigh on you, write down what worries you and what help you need before you talk to anyone. Skip the polish. Just write whatever comes to mind.
PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p1_title: Before you talk to anyone, put your situation on paper
PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p1_why: The fuzzier a money worry, the harder it is to raise. Put it on paper first, and you'll see what to ask for and who to ask.
PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p2_how: Choose one worry about spending or living costs and ask a trusted person who isn't directly involved for their take. A simple 'What would you do?' is all it takes.
PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p2_title: Get an outside view from someone who isn't involved
PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p2_why: Running the numbers alone makes worries snowball, but a fresh pair of eyes often spots a surprisingly simple answer. You learn that even everyday problems ease when you lean on someone.
PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p3_how: Before you open your bank or card statement, lean back in your chair and pause to slow your breathing. If it won't slow much, that's fine. Simply rest your attention on each breath coming and going.
PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p3_title: Slow your breathing for a moment
PRAC_LEAN_MONEY.p3_why: A tense body makes numbers look scarier than they are. Slowing your breath settles your mind enough to look at them calmly.

PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p1_how: Write your name in the center. Around it, add a friend who's easy to call on a rough day, someone who'd cheer you on when you try something new, and places (not only people) that settle your mind. Leave any blank spots open for the future to fill.
PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p1_title: On one page, map where you turn on hard days and who cheers you on
PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p1_why: With people you can count on, you rest more deeply and venture further. Seeing your support network on paper gives you the courage to reach out.
PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p2_how: If something's been hard lately, don't jump straight to asking anyone to fix it. First tell a friend you trust where you are: 'I've been having a rough time lately.' No long explanation needed.
PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p2_title: Don't keep it in: start by saying you're struggling
PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p2_why: Asking for help starts with letting someone know you're having a hard time. Even one person knowing makes you feel far less alone.
PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p3_how: Send a light hello to a friend who's crossed your mind after a long while, and add 'Reply whenever it suits you.' Your promise in this practice: don't wait on the answer, however long it takes.
PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p3_title: Send a check-in that asks for no reply
PRAC_LEAN_SOCIAL.p3_why: A no-pressure check-in keeps the thread of a friendship intact, even loosely. With that thread in place, leaning on each other comes easily when you need it.

PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p1_how: Think back to a recent clash with a coworker and sort your thoughts into 'hard facts' and 'my opinion.' Then find one part of their view that might hold up, and write it in a single line.
PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p1_title: After a disagreement, find one piece of their view that rings true
PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p1_why: Needing to be right in order to feel secure actually leaves you easier to rattle. Concede one small point, and you both find room to return to the table.
PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p2_how: Talk shop with the coworker you clashed with as you normally would, and slip in a little appreciation: "Your notes made this so much easier." No need to rehash what happened.
PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p2_title: Warm the air with a small word of appreciation
PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p2_why: One small comment often melts the awkwardness after a conflict. As appreciation flows both ways, working together feels warm again.
PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p3_how: On a day when something at work got to you, choose one action on your way home that separates you from the job, like washing your hands or changing your clothes. Each time you do it, tell yourself, "That's it for work today."
PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p3_title: Create a ritual that signals 'work mode off'
PRAC_REPAIR_CAREER.p3_why: Carry work feelings home, and you leave yourself less room to recover. A clear switch-off signal makes it far easier to regroup.

PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p1_how: In one line, write down a recent conflict with family and how it turned out. Then find two things you did that shaped the outcome, and note one small thing you'll try differently next time.
PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p1_title: Find two ways your efforts made a difference in a past conflict
PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p1_why: Even when things don't turn out perfectly, your efforts still count. See that clearly, and the next step comes into view instead of helplessness.
PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p2_how: If sitting face to face with a family member after an argument feels awkward, invite them along to the grocery store or on a walk around the neighborhood. Walking side by side, you never have to bring up what happened.
PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p2_title: If talking is hard, start by walking side by side
PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p2_why: Walking side by side often feels easier than a face-to-face talk. Moving together becomes the bridge that reconnects you.
PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p3_how: When a family member says something sharp, skip firing back or going quiet. Take a breath and ask, "Did something happen?" This isn't about swallowing it. It's practice in hitting pause before the rift grows.
PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p3_title: Before you snap back at a sharp comment, ask "Did something happen?"
PRAC_REPAIR_FAMILY.p3_why: Fire back at sharp words, and a full-blown argument follows fast. Ask what's going on first, and you give yourselves a chance to stop before anyone gets hurt more deeply.

PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p1_how: Imagine a dear friend just missed out on an exam or an application, the same way you did. Write a few lines of what you'd say to them. Then choose one line and read it aloud to yourself.
PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p1_title: Write what you'd say to a friend, then read one line to yourself
PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p1_why: Turn the kind words you'd easily offer a friend back toward yourself, and self-blame loosens its grip. The strength to rise again comes from kindness far more than from pushing harder.
PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p2_how: Pick one goal that's felt stuck lately, and list just two other ways to reach it besides what you're doing now. They don't have to be routes you can take right away.
PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p2_title: Map two possible routes for one stuck goal
PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p2_why: Hope isn't blind optimism. It's believing there's a way through. Spot even one other path, and you start moving again after a setback.
PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p3_how: On a day things didn't go your way, put on a song you love and slowly stretch your neck, shoulders, and lower back until it ends. Forget about doing it right. Move only as far as feels good.
PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p3_title: Stretch for the length of one favorite song
PRAC_REPAIR_GROWTH.p3_why: Disappointment settles into your body, too. Loosen up physically first, and your mind follows.

PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p1_how: Write down one label that tends to stick to how you act in arguments, like 'nagging' or 'distant.' Then rewrite what you were truly hoping for in a single sentence: "What I really wanted was..." You're not erasing the impact of what you did, just uncovering the wish underneath it.
PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p1_title: Reframe how you act in arguments as 'What I really wanted was...'
PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p1_why: Even nagging or distance often carries a wish to feel close. Recognize that wish, and you find the words to reach out again after a fight.
PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p2_how: While things are calm between you, make a pact with your partner: "If things get heated, let's take a short break and come back to it." The key is agreeing together on how long the break lasts and when you'll pick it back up.
PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p2_title: Agree to take a time-out when emotions run high
PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p2_why: When you agree on a pause ahead of time, stepping away no longer feels like abandonment. Talk once you've both cooled off, and you're far more likely to make up.
PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p3_how: When you're still fuming after an argument, sit somewhere comfortable, close your eyes, and rest your attention on your breath moving in and out. If thoughts drift in, return to your breathing.
PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p3_title: Close your eyes for a moment and simply breathe
PRAC_REPAIR_LOVE.p3_why: Calm your body first, and your mind settles with it. Once you've caught your breath, you hear the other person out with more generosity.

PRAC_REPAIR_MONEY.p1_how: On a day you overspent or your budget went off the rails, if "What's wrong with me?" pops into your head, write two lines instead: "That part didn't go great" and "Next time, I'll try this." Keep the disappointment; drop the put-downs.
PRAC_REPAIR_MONEY.p1_title: Turn a self-critical thought into two lines: 'what I regret + next time'
PRAC_REPAIR_MONEY.p1_why: "That part didn't go great" and "What's wrong with me?" are worlds apart. Ease up on self-blame, and you keep the energy to adjust your spending next time.
PRAC_REPAIR_MONEY.p2_how: List the everyday chores you've been putting off that keep nagging at you, like canceling a subscription you don't use, sorting receipts, or checking a bill you've been avoiding. Pick the smallest, easiest one, get it done this week, and jot down one line about how it felt.
PRAC_REPAIR_MONEY.p2_title: Pick the smallest task on your put-off list and finish it this week
PRAC_REPAIR_MONEY.p2_why: Little tasks you've put off for ages take up a surprising amount of mental space. Cross just one off, and you feel back in control of your life.
PRAC_REPAIR_MONEY.p3_how: If you spent even a few minutes today doing nothing at all, write it down and label it 'recovery time.' This is how you remind yourself, in writing, that rest that costs nothing still counts as recovery.
PRAC_REPAIR_MONEY.p3_why: Doing nothing is often exactly what helps you recover. Name it, and you enjoy that calm without the guilt.

PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p1_how: Think of one meetup or conversation with a friend that went sideways, and write three lines: what you said, how you felt, and what you'd like to say next time. Start with one thing you did well before you get to what didn't go smoothly.
PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p1_title: Replay a recent get-together: 'what I said, how I felt, what I'd say next time'
PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p1_why: Look back slowly, and you see what went right first, while the rough spots become material for next time. Instead of beating yourself up, you turn toward mending things.
PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p2_how: Recall a phrase or moment you used to laugh about with a friend you've drifted from, and send it as a light way to check in. A short message is all it takes, with no long apology or explanation.
PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p2_title: Bring back something you used to laugh about together
PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p2_why: Shared laughter is one of the best icebreakers there is. One light message can be exactly what brings you back in touch.
PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p3_how: On a day someone has left you upset, make a cup of warm tea or a drink you love, and sip it slowly, taking in its aroma and warmth. Set your phone aside while you drink.
PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p3_title: Slow down and savor a drink
PRAC_REPAIR_SOCIAL.p3_why: When your mind is tangled, tune in to your senses and let your racing thoughts slow down. Pause to soothe yourself, and you gather the strength to reach out again.

PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p1_how: Before a meeting, write down one thing you want to confirm or raise, framed as a question. Something like "Here's how I understood this part. Did I get that right?" slips in easily.
PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p1_title: Prepare one question for your next meeting
PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p1_why: With your words ready, you can bring it up even after the moment passes. That one line you wrote ahead of time is where your voice begins.
PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p2_how: At your next meeting, voice one short opinion out loud, like "I like that direction too." Agreeing or asking a question is a real contribution.
PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p2_title: Start small: share one opinion in a meeting
PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p2_why: Say even one small thing, and the next time gets easier. Bit by bit, you feel your voice belongs in the room.
PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p3_how: If deadlines look tight or work is about to pile up, give the person in charge a quick update before it snowballs. Offer an alternative with it: "I can't finish this by Friday, but here's what will work."
PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p3_title: Give a heads-up before work piles up
PRAC_SPEAK_CAREER.p3_why: The longer you sit on a tough situation, the harder it is to raise and the bigger the cleanup. Flagging it early isn't making excuses. It's valuable information for the people you work with.

PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p1_how: Write down how your family usually handles it when something feels off. Then lay the options side by side: talking it out directly, putting it in writing, asking another family member for help, or giving it time. Star the one that fits best right now, and if you're ready, try it once.
PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p1_title: Find the way of clearing the air that suits your family
PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p1_why: Every family has its own way of working through hard feelings. Choose the approach that fits yours, and speaking up feels far lighter.
PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p2_how: When something a family member does bothers you, put your own feelings front and center. Instead of "Why do you always do that?" try "It hurts a little when I hear that." Share one thing at a time.
PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p2_title: Lead with your feelings instead of blame
PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p2_why: Blame turns a conversation into a fight fast. Share how you feel instead, and you give your family the chance to understand where you're coming from.
PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p3_how: When anger surges while you're talking with family, hold your words. Pause, take a step back, and let out a long breath. Then picture the outcome you want and choose your words from there.
PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p3_title: When you feel yourself flaring up, try 'pause, then step back' once
PRAC_SPEAK_FAMILY.p3_why: The closer the relationship, the faster words fly out before you think. Pause for a beat, and you take back the choice of what to say.

PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p1_how: Before you talk to anyone about what you want to do or where your path is heading, write your thoughts down as they come. Then underline the one sentence you most want to get across.
PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p1_title: Write it out before you talk it out, and get clear on how you feel
PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p1_why: On paper, a fuzzy feeling turns clear. Hold one clear sentence, and you find the courage to say it out loud.
PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p2_how: If you're starting or trying something new this week, give a quick heads-up to one person who'll cheer you on: "I'm going to give this a shot." No need to ask for advice.
PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p2_title: Tell one person in your corner when you try something new
PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p2_why: Telling one person in your corner that you're beginning gives you real momentum. It's also practice in saying your plans out loud.
PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p3_how: Choose one sentence that steadies you when you start to wobble during your preparations, and record it clearly as a voice memo. Listen once a day, and if it's hard to believe, tweak it until it rings true.
PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p3_title: Record a sentence that has your back, then play it back
PRAC_SPEAK_GROWTH.p3_why: A steady voice grows stronger with practice, just as an anxious one does. Take your own side, in your own voice, and you carry that strength into every room you speak in.

PRAC_SPEAK_LOVE.p1_how: Pick one moment in a relationship when you got angry or went cold. Write one word for the feeling that showed on the outside, one word for the more tender feeling underneath, and one sentence for what that feeling was trying to say. If the deeper feeling won't come, "not sure" is a perfectly good answer.
PRAC_SPEAK_LOVE.p1_title: In a moment of anger, write three lines: 'surface feeling / deeper feeling / what I wanted to say'
PRAC_SPEAK_LOVE.p1_why: Anger on the surface often hides hurt or worry underneath. Find what you truly feel, and you can say what you actually meant.
PRAC_SPEAK_LOVE.p2_how: When something stings, open with "I felt hurt when..." before you get into what the other person did. Stick to one moment and keep it short.
PRAC_SPEAK_LOVE.p2_title: Start with "I felt hurt when..." instead of "Why didn't you..."
PRAC_SPEAK_LOVE.p2_why: Opening with "why" tends to put people on the defensive. Lead with your own feelings, and the other person opens up to listen.
PRAC_SPEAK_LOVE.p3_how: Tell your partner, or someone you're getting to know, about one specific thing they did that you appreciated. Keep it short: "I loved that you texted me first today."
PRAC_SPEAK_LOVE.p3_why: Kind thoughts only land when you say them out loud. Let warm words flow back and forth, and the hard conversations feel far less nerve-racking.

PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p1_how: Pick one awkward money topic, like splitting the bill, money you lent, or sharing living costs. Write two or three lines of back-and-forth: what the other person might say and how you'll reply. Read it out loud and keep trimming until you like how it sounds.
PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p1_title: Write a two- or three-line script for a tough conversation
PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p1_why: The hardest part of a money conversation is the moment before you start. Write even a few lines in advance, and the words you've been swallowing become sentences you can actually say.
PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p2_how: When you're making plans to get together, be the first to suggest two options that fit your budget and schedule. Keep it breezy: "How about one of these two?"
PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p2_title: Narrow it down to two options
PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p2_why: You can get your needs across without explaining your finances. Simply making the first suggestion spares you spending that feels like a stretch.
PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p3_how: On days money worries weigh on you, tell someone you trust how you're doing, even briefly: "Money's been tight lately and it's on my mind." They don't need to fix it.
PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p3_title: Put a feeling into words, even just "I'm a little worn out today"
PRAC_SPEAK_MONEY.p3_why: Unspoken worries grow in the dark. Say them out loud, even briefly, and you lighten the load and open the door to asking for help.

PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p1_how: After a chat with a friend or on your way home from a get-together, give what you're feeling a one-word name. The shorter the better: "proud," "hurt," "drained."
PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p1_title: Sum up how you feel in one word
PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p1_why: Name a feeling, and a vague mood starts to untangle. Know what's going on inside first, and sharing it with others comes more easily.
PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p2_how: Write down what you want to say to a friend as it comes, then separate the venting from the parts they truly need to hear. Polish only what you'll share into a sentence or two.
PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p2_title: Split what you want to say into 'what I feel / what I'll actually say'
PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p2_why: Pouring out everything sometimes leaves you both hurt. Choose the words that truly matter, and you say them with calm.
PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p3_how: When your group makes plans and you have a preference about the food, the place, or the time, mention it casually at least once. "I'd kind of prefer this one" is all it takes.
PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p3_title: Speak up lightly instead of bottling it up
PRAC_SPEAK_SOCIAL.p3_why: Swallow enough small opinions, and resentment quietly builds. Share little things lightly and often, and you lay the groundwork for raising the big ones.

PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p1_how: If a work worry is still on your mind at the end of the day, don't force a solution now. Simply jot down, 'This worry is still here.' Then set a time to come back to it.
PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p1_title: Don't solve it tonight: just note 'this worry is still here'
PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p1_why: Naming a feeling puts distance between you and it. Once you've set a time to check back, your mind is free to rest until then.
PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p2_how: For anything you didn't wrap up today, write down the single first thing to do tomorrow. Keep it tiny, like 'open the file.'
PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p2_title: Mark the next step on anything unfinished
PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p2_why: Unfinished tasks love to loop in your head. Write down the next step, and your mind can set that task down for a while.
PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p3_how: When tension creeps in at work, lift your shoulders toward your ears and let them drop, then slowly tilt your head from side to side. A few moments at your desk is enough.
PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p3_title: Release tight spots like your neck and shoulders
PRAC_TRUST_CAREER.p3_why: Worry often lands in your body before you notice it. Release that physical tension, and your mind catches its breath too.

PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p1_how: Write down one family situation you can't change right now, and beside it, one thing you can still do. This isn't about giving up on what you can change.
PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p1_title: Next to what you can't change, write 'what I can still do'
PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p1_why: Family worries pull in things far beyond your control. Pour your energy into the one thing you can do, and you loosen your grip on the rest.
PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p2_how: Instead of calling or visiting family whenever it happens to come up, set regular times, like 'a call on weekend evenings.' It doesn't have to be long. Consistency is what counts.
PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p2_title: Stay in touch on a schedule, not on a whim
PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p2_why: Knowing when you'll next connect takes the edge off the worry in between. A predictable rhythm of contact is its own source of security.
PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p3_how: Find the most comfortable spot at home and make it cozier with one small touch, like a blanket or a cushion. On days your head feels tangled, simply go and sit there for a while.
PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p3_title: Find the coziest spot in your room
PRAC_TRUST_FAMILY.p3_why: When your body has a place to truly unwind, your mind finds something to lean on too. That spot becomes your sanctum (private refuge) whenever family matters shake you.

PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p1_how: Write down one daunting thing you're preparing for. Then write something from your past that felt just as hard but that you got through, and how you did it. Choose one piece of that approach to use this time.
PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p1_title: Link something daunting to something you've already done, in one line
PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p1_why: Even what feels brand new shares something with challenges you've already met. Remembering what you've pulled off gives you solid ground for trusting yourself.
PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p2_how: Write down one study or prep plan for this week, and ask yourself honestly whether you can pull it off. If you're unsure, rewrite it with less time or a smaller goal. On days it doesn't happen, don't call it laziness. Read it as a sign the plan needs resizing.
PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p2_title: Shrink your plan until it feels doable
PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p2_why: An oversized plan turns every missed day into self-blame. Keep your plans to a size you can honor, and your trust in yourself grows steadfast.
PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p3_how: Before you start studying, or whenever anxiety rises, silently name a few things you can see, then a few things you can touch. Finish by feeling your feet on the floor.
PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p3_title: Ground yourself in the present: first what you see, then what you touch
PRAC_TRUST_GROWTH.p3_why: When your head races ahead with worry, your senses bring you back to the here and now. From there, you return easily to what you can do right now.

PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p1_how: If you're getting to know or seeing someone, look back over recent days and write one line each: a moment they responded to your message or story, and a moment you felt on edge. This isn't a test of the relationship. It's practice in noticing what feels comfortable to you.
PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p1_title: Note when the person you're getting to know responded, and when you felt on edge
PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p1_why: Security grows from steady moments of being answered, more than from how strong the butterflies are. Seeing those moments with your own eyes keeps anxious guesses from sweeping you away.
PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p2_how: Give each other a heads-up about which days look busy, and agree on whether lighter texting is okay on those days. A quick chat is all it takes.
PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p2_title: Tell each other your busiest day next week
PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p2_why: When messages slow down and you don't know why, your mind races to the worst. A heads-up turns the wait into something easy.
PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p3_how: Choose one place or moment where you felt truly at ease, and write one line each for what you saw, heard, smelled, and felt. Keep it short, so you can call it up in a heartbeat when waiting for a reply makes you anxious.
PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p3_title: Fill a calming place with all your senses
PRAC_TRUST_LOVE.p3_why: A go-to place where your mind can rest gives you somewhere to return when anxiety rises. This is how you practice calming yourself, whatever the other person does.

PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p1_how: Write down everything about money and daily life that weighs on you, in whatever order it comes. Group similar items, then choose the two that matter most. Move the rest to a 'deal with later' list.
PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p1_title: Pour out every worry, then pick just the top two
PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p1_why: When worries arrive all at once, everything feels urgent. Keep only the top two in hand, and you set the rest aside for now.
PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p2_how: If money worries surface while you're working or relaxing and you feel the urge to check your balance, tell yourself, 'Just a worry passing through.' Let the worry be, and rest your eyes on one specific spot in whatever you were doing.
PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p2_title: When worry butts in, return your eyes to one spot in your task
PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p2_why: You can carry on with what you were doing without battling the worry. Each time you delay that check a little, the feeling of being chased fades.
PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p3_how: This week, keep your bedtime and wake-up time about the same each day. The key is not drifting far from them on weekends, either.
PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p3_title: Build a rhythm of sleeping and waking at the same time
PRAC_TRUST_MONEY.p3_why: Money worries rarely resolve overnight, but your daily rhythm is a source of stability you truly own. Steady your body, and your mind steadies with it.

PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p1_how: If a thought like 'Do they dislike me?' pops up after a get-together, come up with two other explanations for that moment before you settle on it. They were tired, or their mind was on something else.
PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p1_title: Before you decide it's true, consider other explanations
PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p1_why: Anxiety grabs the worst explanation first. Simply leaving room for other possibilities opens space to trust the friendship.
PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p2_how: If it's a gathering or event you've never been to, decide ahead of time how you'll get home and when you'll head out. Leaving earlier than planned is perfectly fine.
PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p2_title: Plan your way home before a new get-together
PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p2_why: When you can see the finish line, a new setting feels far less overwhelming. Inside a safety net you've built yourself, you relax and enjoy it.
PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p3_how: After seeing people, note one conversation topic that felt especially good. Write it down first, before any moment you wish had gone differently.
PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p3_title: Remember one great conversation after seeing people
PRAC_TRUST_SOCIAL.p3_why: After a get-together, the awkward moments tend to linger longest. Record the good ones, and you build a store of memories of feeling at ease around people.

TERM_ASC.detail: Your Ascendant is the sign that was rising on the eastern horizon when you were born. It shows the aura people sense when they first meet you and how you approach the world.
TERM_ASC.meaning_line: How you come across, the first impression you make, and your body's natural rhythm.

TERM_CONJ.detail: A conjunction happens when two planets meet at nearly the same point. It's the strongest aspect, and how it plays out depends on which planets are involved.
TERM_CONJ.meaning_line: Two planets sit together, and their energies blend at full strength.

TERM_H01.detail: This house is all about you: your identity, your body's rhythm, and the impression you make. When a planet passes through, the way you see yourself and come across shifts.
TERM_H01.meaning_line: Who you are, the first impression you make, and how you show up in the world.

TERM_H02.detail: This house rules money, possessions, and self-worth. When a planet passes through, you rethink what truly matters to you and how you handle money.
TERM_H02.meaning_line: Money, the things you own, and how much you value yourself.

TERM_H03.detail: This house covers everyday learning, conversation, and keeping in touch with the people around you. When a planet passes through, ideas tend to flow and learning picks up.

TERM_H04.detail: This house covers home, family, and wherever you go to recharge. When a planet passes through, you think more deeply about your living space and what makes you feel secure.
TERM_H04.meaning_line: Covers home, family, and your emotional roots.

TERM_H05.detail: This house is about what lights you up: play, hobbies, creative projects, and romance. When a planet passes through, it's a great time to rediscover what gets you excited.
TERM_H05.meaning_line: Fun, romance, creativity, and anything that gives you butterflies.

TERM_H06.detail: This house rules the day-to-day: regular tasks, habits, and taking care of your body. When a planet passes through, you fine-tune your daily rhythm and the way you work.
TERM_H06.meaning_line: Your daily work, routines, and habits that keep your body well.

TERM_H07.detail: This house covers one-on-one relationships, from close colleagues to romantic partners. When a planet passes through, you start weighing the give-and-take in your relationships.

TERM_H08.detail: This house covers relationships built on deep trust, shared resources, and inner transformation. A planet passing through gives you the chance to work through feelings you've kept buried for a long time.
TERM_H08.meaning_line: Deep bonds, shared resources, and profound inner change.

TERM_H09.detail: This house covers long-distance travel, in-depth study, and your outlook on life. When a planet passes through, you feel a stronger pull to broaden your horizons.
TERM_H09.meaning_line: Higher learning, travel, and the values you live by.

TERM_H10.detail: This house covers your public role and what you achieve at work. When a planet passes through, questions about your career path or responsibilities tend to come up.
TERM_H10.meaning_line: Your career, public role, and where your work is headed.

TERM_H11.detail: This house covers friends, groups, and the future you're building together. When a planet passes through, it's a good time to think about who you want by your side and where you want to go.
TERM_H11.meaning_line: Your people, your community, and your hopes for the future.

TERM_H12.detail: This house covers time alone, rest, and inner processing. When a planet passes through, you quietly prepare for what's next, away from the spotlight.
TERM_H12.meaning_line: Rest, your inner world, and the work that happens behind the scenes.

TERM_INGRESS.detail: An ingress is the moment a planet leaves one sign and enters the next. The slower the planet, the longer the new mood it sets in motion.
TERM_INGRESS.meaning_line: A planet crosses into the next sign, and the mood shifts.

TERM_JUPITER.detail: Jupiter stands for growth and opportunity. Wherever it travels in your chart, your outlook and experiences expand.
TERM_JUPITER.meaning_line: Where your world opens up and opportunities come your way.

TERM_LUNAR_ECLIPSE.detail: A lunar eclipse happens when Earth's shadow falls across the Moon, and in astrology it marks the close of a chapter. Use it to sort out what to let go of and what to keep.
TERM_LUNAR_ECLIPSE.meaning_line: The day the Moon goes dark, a cue to look at what you're ready to wrap up.

TERM_MARS.detail: Mars governs motivation, action, and drive. It shows how much force and speed you bring when you start something and push it forward.
TERM_MARS.meaning_line: What fires you up, and how you turn that energy into action.

TERM_MC.detail: The Midheaven is the highest point in the sky at the moment you were born. It points to what you'd like to be known for and where your work is headed.
TERM_MC.meaning_line: Where your work and public role are headed.

TERM_MERCURY.detail: Mercury governs thinking, speaking, learning, and communication. It shows how you take in information and put your thoughts into words.
TERM_MERCURY.meaning_line: How you think, talk, and stay in touch.
TERM_MERCURY.nickname: The planet of thought and speech

TERM_MOON.detail: The Moon rules your feelings and emotional security. It shows you what makes you feel safe and what throws you off balance.
TERM_MOON.meaning_line: What helps you feel at ease, and how your emotions ebb and flow.

TERM_NEPTUNE.detail: Neptune stands for dreams, inspiration, and haze. As your imagination grows, the line between fantasy and reality can blur, so double-check things as you go.
TERM_NEPTUNE.meaning_line: Brings dreams and inspiration, but can make the way forward feel foggy for a while.
TERM_NEPTUNE.nickname: The planet of haze and dreams

TERM_OPPOSITION.detail: An opposition forms when two planets sit on opposite sides of the sky. You feel pulled in two directions, and that tug-of-war teaches you to find balance.
TERM_OPPOSITION.meaning_line: Two planets face off from opposite sides, asking you to find your balance.

TERM_PLUTO.detail: Pluto stands for deep transformation and rebirth. Its influence is slow but profound, clearing out the old so something new can emerge.
TERM_PLUTO.meaning_line: Deep, slow-burning transformation from the inside out.

TERM_RETURN.detail: A return happens when a planet completes its orbit and comes back to the same spot in your birth chart. It's a chance to wrap up the last cycle in that area of life and get ready for the next one.
TERM_RETURN.meaning_line: A planet comes back to where it was when you were born, a moment to look back over a full cycle.

TERM_RX.detail: A planet goes retrograde when, seen from Earth, it seems to move backward for a while. It's better for reviewing and fixing what that planet rules than for starting anything new.
TERM_RX.meaning_line: When a planet appears to move backward, a cue to revisit the parts of life it rules.
TERM_RX.nickname: When things seem to go backward

TERM_SATURN.detail: Saturn stands for responsibility, structure, and tests. Its transits feel weighty, and they leave you standing on firmer ground.
TERM_SATURN.meaning_line: Asks you to take stock of the structure and responsibilities in your life.

TERM_SEXTILE.detail: In a sextile, two planets give each other a friendly boost. The help is real, but it works best when you meet it halfway.
TERM_SEXTILE.meaning_line: Two planets team up lightly and open doors for you.

TERM_SOLAR_ECLIPSE.detail: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon blocks the Sun, and in astrology it marks the start of a new chapter. Instead of rushing into anything, take time to jot down what you'd like to grow from here.
TERM_SOLAR_ECLIPSE.meaning_line: The day the Sun goes dark, a cue to think about what you'd like to begin.

TERM_SQUARE.detail: A square forms when two planets pull in different directions. It feels uncomfortable at times, but that friction sparks change and growth.
TERM_SQUARE.meaning_line: Two planets clash and create pressure, but that pressure gets you moving.

TERM_SUN.detail: The Sun represents your core drive and the direction your sense of self is heading. Its sign and house show how you want to shine.
TERM_SUN.meaning_line: Your sense of self, and the kind of person you want to be at heart.

TERM_TRANSIT.detail: A transit is when a planet in the actual sky right now forms an angle with a planet in your birth chart. Most timing in your reading is based on transits.
TERM_TRANSIT.meaning_line: When planets moving through today's sky activate points in your birth chart.

TERM_TRINE.detail: In a trine, two planets share the same element and support each other naturally. Things tend to flow with little effort on your part.
TERM_TRINE.meaning_line: Two planets are in sync, helping things run smoothly.

TERM_URANUS.detail: Uranus stands for sudden change and turning points. It shakes things up, and it also opens the door to new offers, new roles, or a different path.
TERM_URANUS.meaning_line: Brings surprise turns and fresh possibilities.

TERM_VENUS.detail: Venus governs what you love, your relationships, and your sense of money. It helps you see what brings you joy and which relationships feel like home.
TERM_VENUS.meaning_line: What you love, how you connect with people, and how you handle money.
TERM_VENUS.nickname: The planet of pleasure and relationships

ING_CHIRON.text: As the planet of healing enters {{하우스영역}}, it's a time to begin learning how to care for old hurts in this area.

ING_JUPITER.text: As the planet of expansion enters {{하우스영역}}, things here begin to widen and opportunities start to grow.

ING_NEPTUNE.text: As the planet of dreams enters {{하우스영역}}, the way you see this part of your life can grow softer and wider.

ING_NOTIME.text: As {{행성}} moves into a new sign, a mood that may stay with you for a while begins to take shape.

ING_PLUTO.text: As the planet of rebirth enters {{하우스영역}}, a deep, long-lasting change slowly begins.

ING_SATURN.text: As the planet of responsibility enters {{하우스영역}}, it's a time to start building firm footing here.

ING_URANUS.text: As the planet of change enters {{하우스영역}}, familiar ways of doing things begin to shift into something new.

QB_BOUND_01.headline_q: Where will you draw the line to keep your life steady?
QB_BOUND_01.q1: Think of a time you said yes to a favor and felt uneasy about it long afterward.
QB_BOUND_01.q2: What time or space do you need to protect to keep your days on an even keel?
QB_BOUND_01.q3: Is there something you'd like to politely turn down? How will you put it?
QB_BOUND_01.why_template: If holding boundaries wears you out, saying yes to everyone else quietly costs you the stability of your own routine. {{기질문장}} If stability is what you want, start by deciding what you won't take on, before you think about what to add.

QB_BOUND_02.headline_q: What will you say no to, and what will you go all in on, to make your leap?
QB_BOUND_02.q1: When did your own plans last get pushed aside while you helped with someone else's work? What got put on hold?
QB_BOUND_02.q2: If you could pick just one thing to focus on, what would it be?
QB_BOUND_02.q3: To protect that, what will you cut back on or turn down?
QB_BOUND_02.why_template: When boundaries are hard to hold, saying yes to every request scatters the time and energy your big leap needs. {{기질문장}} Gather your strength in one place, and remember: every no you say is also a step forward.

QB_BOUND_03.headline_q: What boundaries do you need so you can actually recover?
QB_BOUND_03.q1: Recall a day you meant to rest but couldn't because of messages or requests.
QB_BOUND_03.q2: When do you want time that's entirely your own?
QB_BOUND_03.q3: On a tired day, what's the easiest way for you to say 'Today doesn't work for me'?
QB_BOUND_03.why_template: Setting limits takes a lot out of you. Even when you're running on empty, you put others' requests first and miss your chance to recharge. {{기질문장}} If recovery is your wish, draw a firm line around your downtime. That is the most practical self-care there is.

QB_BOUND_04.headline_q: In love, where's the line that keeps you, you?
QB_BOUND_04.q1: Think of a time you bent so far for someone close that you felt you'd lost yourself.
QB_BOUND_04.q2: Even in a loving relationship, what time or space do you want to keep just for you?
QB_BOUND_04.q3: How could you tell someone you care about 'This is hard for me' without hurting their feelings?
QB_BOUND_04.why_template: If boundaries don't come easily, the closer the relationship, the more you hesitate to say no for fear of hurting someone. {{기질문장}} A healthy boundary isn't a wall that pushes people away. Think of it as a garden fence: it lets you stay close for the long haul.

QB_BOUND_05.headline_q: Who will you keep close, and who at a comfortable distance?
QB_BOUND_05.q1: Which relationship leaves you most drained? When does your energy dip?
QB_BOUND_05.q2: Who's someone you've said no to without it hurting the relationship?
QB_BOUND_05.q3: Which relationships deserve more of your time, and which a little less?
QB_BOUND_05.why_template: When drawing lines feels draining, you end up giving every relationship the same energy, with little left for the people who matter most. {{기질문장}} Keep different distances with different people. That is how you grow closer to the kindred spirits you treasure.

QB_BOUND_06.headline_q: What will you take off your plate to give yourself breathing room?
QB_BOUND_06.q1: What's a task you took on even while thinking, 'This isn't really my job'?
QB_BOUND_06.q2: Picture a stretch of time with nothing on your calendar. What would you love to do with it?
QB_BOUND_06.q3: What role could you let go of, just this once?
QB_BOUND_06.why_template: If saying no is hard for you, your calendar fills up with things you couldn't turn down until there's no breathing room left. {{기질문장}} Breathing room doesn't simply appear when you have spare time. You create it by separating what's yours to carry from what belongs to someone else.

QB_BOUND_07.headline_q: What will you draw the line at to protect your daily rhythm?
QB_BOUND_07.q1: Recall a day when late-night messages or last-minute plans threw off your routine.
QB_BOUND_07.q2: What daily basics, like your bedtime or mealtimes, matter most to you?
QB_BOUND_07.q3: To protect those basics, what would you like to tell the people around you up front?
QB_BOUND_07.why_template: For you, boundaries take effort, and fitting into everyone else's schedule throws off the basics first, like sleep and meals. {{기질문장}} Healthy living means adding new habits, yes, but it starts with guarding the routines you already have.

QB_BOUND_08.headline_q: When it comes to money, what's really yours to cover?
QB_BOUND_08.q1: Think of money you spent because you couldn't say no. How did it feel?
QB_BOUND_08.q2: If you set your own rules for social spending, like group outings or gifts, what would they be?
QB_BOUND_08.q3: What spending will you cut back on to feel more at ease day to day?
QB_BOUND_08.why_template: When holding boundaries is hard, protecting relationships pushes you past the limits of your own budget. {{기질문장}} Financial ease comes from earning, and just as much from deciding for yourself how far you're willing to spend. Set that line now.

QB_BOUND_09.headline_q: What line won't you cross, even for recognition?
QB_BOUND_09.q1: Think of a time you took on too much because you wanted to be recognized. What comes to mind?
QB_BOUND_09.q2: Picture someone who says no and is still respected. How do they put it?
QB_BOUND_09.q3: Where do you want to show what you can do, and what would you rather politely decline?
QB_BOUND_09.why_template: If boundaries take effort, the more you want recognition, the more readily you say yes to unreasonable requests. {{기질문장}} Be clear about what you can and can't take on. People come to see you as more dependable, not less.

QB_BOUND_10.headline_q: What line keeps you true to yourself?
QB_BOUND_10.q1: Recall living up to someone else's expectations and catching yourself thinking, 'This isn't me.'
QB_BOUND_10.q2: What value would you refuse to give up, no matter what anyone says?
QB_BOUND_10.q3: Recall a time you held a line that felt true to you. What feeling stays with you?
QB_BOUND_10.why_template: When limits are hard to set, you lose sight of what you want while you're busy adjusting to others. {{기질문장}} Each time you decide for yourself what to accept and what to turn down, your sense of self comes into sharper focus.

QB_BOUND_11.headline_q: What will you let go of to make a fresh start?
QB_BOUND_11.q1: Think of a time you wanted to start something new, but your existing commitments kept getting in the way.
QB_BOUND_11.q2: What time or space would you like to keep clear for a fresh start?
QB_BOUND_11.q3: What role or promise are you ready to gracefully step away from?
QB_BOUND_11.why_template: If saying no wears you out, you carry every old favor and role along with you, leaving little room for something new. {{기질문장}} Room for a fresh start opens the moment you decide what to release, not just what to add.

QB_LEAN_01.headline_q: Who will you build stability with?
QB_LEAN_01.q1: Think of a recent moment when you were getting through something alone and wished someone were there. What was happening?
QB_LEAN_01.q2: Picture an evening when you feel truly at ease. Who's there with you?
QB_LEAN_01.q3: Who would you like to open up to a little more about how things have been, and what would you tell them first?
QB_LEAN_01.why_template: Leaning on others takes a lot out of you, so you tend to build stability entirely on your own. {{기질문장}} Your stability in the year ahead begins less with getting more done and more with finding people who share the load.

QB_LEAN_02.headline_q: Whose hand will you hold to leap higher?
QB_LEAN_02.q1: When you take on something new, who's the first person you turn to for advice or help?
QB_LEAN_02.q2: Think of something you prepared for alone, struggling the whole way. What would have changed if you'd shared it with someone?
QB_LEAN_02.q3: As you take your next step, what specific help will you ask the people around you for?
QB_LEAN_02.why_template: When relying on others doesn't come easily, you tend to prepare for a big leap alone and reveal only the finished result. {{기질문장}} Ask for help early, and the prep feels lighter while your strength to leap grows.

QB_LEAN_03.headline_q: Who can you let yourself be tired around?
QB_LEAN_03.q1: Think of your most exhausting day lately. Who did you want to tell about it?
QB_LEAN_03.q2: Recall a time when simply having someone nearby made you feel lighter. What was that moment like?
QB_LEAN_03.q3: If you could choose just one kind of support for hard times, what would it look like?
QB_LEAN_03.why_template: If asking for support is hard, the more worn out you get, the more you go quiet and recover alone. {{기질문장}} If recovery is your wish, make time not only for rest but for being near people you can truly unwind with.

QB_LEAN_04.headline_q: In love, how will you lean on someone, and let them lean on you?
QB_LEAN_04.q1: When did you want to lean on someone close to you but hold back?
QB_LEAN_04.q2: Think of a moment when you feel loved. What is the other person doing?
QB_LEAN_04.q3: Put one small thing you'd like from someone you love right now into words. What would you say?
QB_LEAN_04.why_template: Even in love, leaning on others costs you energy, so you tend to swallow what you want for fear of being a burden. {{기질문장}} If love is your wish, let someone see, little by little, that you want to lean on them. That openness is your key to growing closer.

QB_LEAN_05.headline_q: Who do you want in your corner, and whose corner will you be in?
QB_LEAN_05.q1: Think of someone you could trade help with, no strings attached. What made that relationship feel so easy?
QB_LEAN_05.q2: Who have you been seeing lately who leaves you feeling lighter?
QB_LEAN_05.q3: Is there someone you'd like to grow closer to? What will you say to them first?
QB_LEAN_05.why_template: For someone who finds leaning on others hard, "good people" aren't the ones you know the most but the ones you can lean on with ease. {{기질문장}} Start by noticing who, among the people already in your life, you can comfortably lean on, and let lean on you.

QB_LEAN_06.headline_q: What will you hand off to give yourself room to breathe?
QB_LEAN_06.q1: Of everything you're carrying alone right now, what could you share with someone else?
QB_LEAN_06.q2: Think of a day when you truly got to rest. What was different about it?
QB_LEAN_06.q3: When you think about handing something off, what thoughts hold you back?
QB_LEAN_06.why_template: Asking for help takes a lot out of you, so you often do everything yourself and lose your breathing room along the way. {{기질문장}} Breathing room comes from taking things off your plate, and just as much from keeping people close you can hand things to.

QB_LEAN_07.headline_q: Who will help you keep your daily rhythm?
QB_LEAN_07.q1: Think of a habit you kept up for a long time. What helped it stick?
QB_LEAN_07.q2: Which routine, like a walk or getting to bed on time, would be easier with someone else?
QB_LEAN_07.q3: When your daily rhythm starts slipping, who can you easily tell?
QB_LEAN_07.why_template: When relying on others feels hard, you tend to keep up your habits on willpower alone and wear yourself out. {{기질문장}} Small agreements, like walking together or texting each other at bedtime, keep a routine alive for the long run.

QB_LEAN_08.headline_q: Who will you share money worries with, and what standards will you set?
QB_LEAN_08.q1: Think of a time you kept crunching the numbers alone over a money problem. What did you need most then?
QB_LEAN_08.q2: Who can you talk to openly about living costs or spending?
